newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PNG mining float said getting strong support.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PNG mining float said getting strong support.

text.p: Orogen Minerals Ltd, the large-scale minerals operation being floated by the Papua New Guinea government, has received indications of strong institutional interest in roadshow presentations, the company said.
Firm bids for A$100 million worth of shares had been received from the Australian and New Zealand public, it said in a statement.
This was ahead of the start of the Asian and U.S. leg of the roadshow presentations, it said.

"Offshore investors are particularly interested in Orogen's unique exposure to the prospectivity of the region which the option agreement provides," Jeremy Tasker, a director of global coordinator Jardine Fleming Ord Minnett, said.

The option between Orogen and the state of Papua New Guinea gives Orogen a preferred right, but not the obligation, to acquire a 25 percent interest in future significant mining development projects and a 20.5 percent interest in future significant petroleum development projects.
The fact that Orogen's assets include several projects which are already operating and producing cash flow is also proving a strong point of interest, Tasker said.

The Asian leg of the road show started on Monday with presentations in Singapore, to be followed by presentations in Hong Kong beginning on Wednesday. The road show then departs for the United States.
Orogen Minerals will have a stake in some of PNG's largest gold and petroleum projects, with the PNG government floating 49 percent of its Mineral Resources Development Corp (MRDC) through Orogen.
The main resource ventures in which MRDC and Orogen have interests are the Kutubu and Gobe oilfields and the Porgera, Misima and Lihir gold mines.

Orogen also has an option agreement to take up the government's non-landowner rights in future mining or petroleum developments as well as in the Ok Tedi and the currently suspended Bougainville copper projects.
Orogen will list on the Australian Stock Exchange on November 1 after a A$261 million share raising.
The retail share offer closes October 23, while the institutional offer, based an open price book build, closes October 30.
